data.title: THE PATRIOT FUND HONORS VETERANS AND MARKS AMERICA'S 250TH AT 11TH ANNUAL GALA AT THE UNION LEAGUE OF PHILADELPHIA
data.description:
THE PATRIOT FUND HONORS VETERANS AND MARKS AMERICA'S 250TH AT 11TH ANNUAL GALA AT THE UNION LEAGUE OF PHILADELPHIA

THE PATRIOT FUND HONORS VETERANS AND MARKS AMERICA'S 250TH AT 11TH ANNUAL GALA AT THE UNION LEAGUE OF PHILADELPHIA

PR Newswire

PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 23, 2026

Army and Navy Veterans headline the evening as Union League past president Frank Giordano is named 2026 Greater Philadelphia Area Patriot of the Year

PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Patriot Fund will bring together Veterans, military families, supporters and community leaders on Friday, October 23, 2026, for the 11th Annual Patriot Fund Gala at the Union League of Philadelphia. Held in the city where our nation was founded, in the year America celebrates its 250th anniversary, this year's gala honors the men and women who have served and the families who stand behind them.

For 11 years, The Patriot Fund has helped Veterans and their families overcome the challenges they face when returning home from service. Support raised through the gala helps the organization fund its vetted, "Best in Class" partner organizations, which deliver essential services and ongoing support to Veterans and their families.

Fittingly, the evening's program will be led by those who have worn the uniform. The Patriot Fund is proud to welcome back Major Jonathan Turnbull, U.S. Army (Ret.), as Keynote Speaker, along with Evangelo "Vann" Morris, U.S. Navy (Ret.), Surface Warfare Officer, as Special Presenter. Guests will also enjoy a cocktail hour, dinner and live music from the band Don't Call Me Francis.

The Patriot Fund will also recognize Frank Giordano, President and CEO of Atlantic Trailer Leasing Corporation, as the 2026 Greater Philadelphia Area Patriot of the Year. Giordano is a longtime member and past president of the Union League of Philadelphia.

"Frank's commitment to preserving and advancing the American story is one of his most admirable traits," said Ryan Peters, who nominated Giordano for the award. "For decades, he has exemplified the highest ideals of American citizenship through his unwavering commitment to community service and his steadfast devotion to the principles on which our nation was founded."

"As the year draws to a close and Veterans Day approaches, we are more grateful than ever for the support our communities have shown us, and in turn, our Veterans," said Matthew Ellison, Executive Director of The Patriot Fund. "Gathering in the city where our country was founded feels especially fitting as we celebrate its 250th anniversary. Every guest and sponsor in that room is helping make sure the Veterans who served this nation, and the families who served alongside them, have the support they need when they come home."

Sponsorship opportunities and event details are available at PF2026.givesmart.com.

ABOUT THE PATRIOT FUND

The Patriot Fund is dedicated to providing the critical funding Veterans need to ensure they and their families have access to essential services and ongoing support throughout their lives. We carefully vet and support only "Best in Class" partners: organizations making a meaningful and measurable difference in the lives of Veterans today. Through our Stories of Impact, we shine a light on the challenges facing our Veteran community and the organizations working to address them.

Contact: Mike Baldini, Baldini Communications
Email: mgbaldini@gobaldinicommunications.com
Phone: 215-870-5548

data.title: Travere Presents New Biomarker Data at ASN Kidney Week Suggesting FILSPARI® (sparsentan) May Modify Underlying Disease Pathophysiology in IgA Nephropathy
data.description:
Travere Presents New Biomarker Data at ASN Kidney Week Suggesting FILSPARI® (sparsentan) May Modify Underlying Disease Pathophysiology in IgA Nephropathy

FILSPARI achieved greater reductions in biomarkers linked to kidney inflammation and injury than maximum labeled dose irbesartan

Findings provide further evidence of the biological effects of dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism and support FILSPARI as foundational treatment in IgAN 

Travere Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TVTX) today presented new biomarker data from the Phase 3 PROTECT Study providing evidence that FILSPARI® (sparsentan) may modify the underlying disease pathophysiology in people with IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Data were shared today in an oral presentation at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, CO.

“These biomarker data provide new insight into how FILSPARI’s dual mechanism of action may modify the underlying biology of IgA nephropathy,” said Jula Inrig, M.D., chief medical officer of Travere Therapeutics. “When considered alongside the PROTECT results which demonstrated superior proteinuria reduction and a slower rate of kidney function decline compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan, as well as published real-world evidence showing consistent outcomes in clinical practice, the totality of evidence supports the use of FILSPARI as a non-immunosuppressive, kidney-targeted, foundational first-line treatment for IgA nephropathy.”

The Phase 3 PROTECT Study was a global, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of FILSPARI, compared to irbesartan in 404 adult patients with IgAN. Of the overall study population, 295 patients participated in the biomarker analysis. Across measured time points through Week 110, FILSPARI led to rapid and sustained reductions in all four urinary biomarkers evaluated.

“These findings extend the exploratory signal observed in SPARTAN and show in a larger, randomized study that dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism may modulate several biological pathways associated with IgAN pathophysiology,” said Chee Kay Cheung, M.B.Ch.B., Ph.D., consultant nephrologist at University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust.

At Week 110, least-squares mean percent changes from baseline, normalized to urine creatinine, were greater with FILSPARI than with irbesartan (reported p values are nominal):

  • sCD163, a marker of macrophage activation, decreased 60.1% with FILSPARI versus 26.0% with irbesartan, representing a 46.1% difference between treatment arms (p<0.001).
  • BAFF, a marker of B-cell activation and survival, decreased 64.4% with FILSPARI versus 45.2% with irbesartan, representing a 34.9% difference between treatment arms (p=0.02).
  • C5b-9, a marker of complement pathway activation, decreased 50.2% with FILSPARI versus 7.3% with irbesartan, representing a 46.3% difference between treatment arms (p=0.032).
  • IL-6, a pro-inflammatory cytokine, decreased 45.4% with FILSPARI versus an 8.7% increase with irbesartan, representing a 49.7% difference between treatment arms (p<0.001).

The findings build on previously reported PROTECT results which demonstrated superior proteinuria reduction and a slower rate of kidney function decline with FILSPARI compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan. The consistency of effects across clinical outcomes and multiple biomarkers associated with IgAN disease biology provides further evidence that FILSPARI’s dual endothelin and angiotensin receptor antagonism may provide benefits beyond conventional RAS inhibition and supports its differentiated profile as an early, foundational, non-immunosuppressive treatment for IgAN.

More information on Travere’s presence at ASN Kidney Week can be found here.

About the PROTECT Study

The Phase 3 PROTECT Study was a global, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of FILSPARI compared with maximum labeled dose irbesartan in 404 adults with biopsy-confirmed IgAN. Participants had urine protein excretion (UPE) ≥1.0 g/d and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² despite optimized renin-angiotensin system inhibitor therapy. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive FILSPARI 400 mg/day or irbesartan 300 mg/day for up to 110 weeks. The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in proteinuria from baseline at Week 36, and the key secondary efficacy endpoint was the rate of change in eGFR through Week 110.

About Travere Therapeutics

At Travere Therapeutics, we are in rare for life. We are a biopharmaceutical company that comes together every day to help patients, families and caregivers of all backgrounds as they navigate life with a rare disease. On this path, we know the need for treatment options is urgent – that is why our global team works with the rare disease community to identify, develop and deliver life-changing therapies. In pursuit of this mission, we continuously seek to understand the diverse perspectives of rare patients and to courageously forge new paths to make a difference in their lives and provide hope – today and tomorrow. For more information, visit travere.com.

FILSPARI® (sparsentan) U.S. Indication

FILSPARI® (sparsentan) is indicated:

  • To slow kidney function decline in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) who are at risk for disease progression.
  • To reduce proteinuria in adult and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) without nephrotic syndrome.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

BOXED WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY AND EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY

Because of the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Under the FILSPARI REMS, prescribers, patients and pharmacies must enroll in the program.

Hepatotoxicity

Some Endothelin Receptor Antagonists (ERAs) have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. In clinical studies, elevations in aminotransferases (ALT or AST) of at least 3-times the Upper Limit of Normal (ULN) have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge.

Measure transaminases and bilirubin before initiating treatment and then every 3 months during treatment. Interrupt treatment and closely monitor patients who develop aminotransferase elevations more than 3x ULN.

FILSPARI should generally be avoided in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) at baseline because monitoring for hepatotoxicity may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity

FILSPARI is contraindicated for use during pregnancy because it may cause fetal harm if used by pregnant patients. Therefore, in patients who can become pregnant, exclude pregnancy prior to initiation of FILSPARI. Advise use of effective contraception before the initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible.

Contraindications

FILSPARI is contraindicated in patients who are pregnant. Do not coadminister FILSPARI with angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), ERAs, or aliskiren.

Warnings and Precautions

  • Hepatotoxicity: Elevations in ALT or AST of at least 3-fold ULN have been observed in up to 3.5% of FILSPARI-treated patients, including cases confirmed with rechallenge. While no concurrent elevations in bilirubin >2-times ULN or cases of liver failure were observed in FILSPARI-treated patients in clinical trials, some ERAs have caused elevations of aminotransferases, hepatotoxicity, and liver failure. To reduce the risk of potential serious hepatotoxicity, measure serum aminotransferase levels and total bilirubin prior to initiation of treatment and then every 3 months during treatment.

    Advise patients with symptoms suggesting hepatotoxicity (nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, fatigue, anorexia, jaundice, dark urine, fever, or itching) to immediately stop treatment with FILSPARI and seek medical attention. If aminotransferase levels are abnormal at any time during treatment, interrupt FILSPARI and monitor as recommended.

    Consider re-initiation of FILSPARI only when hepatic enzyme levels and bilirubin return to pretreatment values and only in patients who have not experienced clinical symptoms of hepatotoxicity. Avoid initiation of FILSPARI in patients with elevated aminotransferases (>3x ULN) because monitoring hepatotoxicity in these patients may be more difficult and these patients may be at increased risk for serious hepatotoxicity.
  • FILSPARI REMS: Due to the risk of hepatotoxicity, FILSPARI is available only through a restricted program called the FILSPARI REMS. Prescribers, patients, and pharmacies must be enrolled in the REMS program and comply with all requirements (www.filsparirems.com).
  • Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Based on data from animal reproduction studies, FILSPARI may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant patient and is contraindicated during pregnancy. The available human data for ERAs do not establish the presence or absence of fetal harm related to the use of FILSPARI. Counsel patients who can become pregnant of the potential risk to a fetus. Exclude pregnancy before initiating treatment with FILSPARI. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for two weeks after discontinuation of treatment with FILSPARI. Advise pre-pubertal females and/or their guardian(s) of the fetal risk and the need to use effective contraception once they reach reproductive potential. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue FILSPARI as soon as possible.
  • Hypotension: Hypotension has been observed in patients treated with ARBs and ERAs and was observed in FILSPARI clinical studies. There was a greater incidence of hypotension-associated adverse events, some serious, including dizziness, in patients treated with FILSPARI compared to irbesartan. In patients at risk for hypotension, consider eliminating or adjusting other antihypertensive medications and maintaining appropriate volume status. If hypotension develops, despite elimination or reduction of other antihypertensive medications, consider a dose reduction or dose interruption of FILSPARI. A transient hypotensive response is not a contraindication to further dosing of FILSPARI, which can be given once blood pressure has stabilized.
  • Acute Kidney Injury: Monitor kidney function periodically. Drugs that inhibit the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) can cause kidney injury. Patients whose kidney function may depend in part on the activity of the RAS (e.g., patients with renal artery stenosis, chronic kidney disease, severe congestive heart failure, or volume depletion) may be at particular risk of developing acute kidney injury on FILSPARI. Consider withholding or discontinuing therapy in patients who develop a clinically significant decrease in kidney function while on FILSPARI.
  • Hyperkalemia: Monitor serum potassium periodically and treat appropriately. Patients with advanced kidney disease, taking concomitant potassium-increasing drugs (e.g., potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics), or using potassium-containing salt substitutes are at increased risk for developing hyperkalemia. Dosage reduction or discontinuation of FILSPARI may be required.
  • Fluid Retention: Fluid retention may occur with ERAs and has been observed in clinical studies with FILSPARI. FILSPARI has not been evaluated in patients with heart failure. If clinically significant fluid retention develops, evaluate the patient to determine the cause and the potential need to initiate or modify the dose of diuretic treatment then consider modifying the dose of FILSPARI.

Adverse Reactions

  • IgAN patients receiving FILSPARI: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are hyperkalemia, hypotension (including orthostatic hypotension), peripheral edema, dizziness, anemia, and acute kidney injury.
  • FSGS patients receiving FILSPARI: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) are peripheral edema, hypotension (including orthostatic hypotension), hyperkalemia, dizziness, and anemia.

Drug Interactions

  • Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS) Inhibitors and ERAs: Do not coadminister FILSPARI with ARBs, ERAs, or aliskiren due to increased risks of hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure).
  • Strong and Moderate CYP3A Inhibitors: Avoid concomitant use of FILSPARI with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor cannot be avoided, interrupt FILSPARI treatment. When resuming treatment with FILSPARI, consider dose titration. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly when used concomitantly with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. Concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inhibitor increases sparsentan exposure which may increase the risk of FILSPARI adverse reactions.
  • Strong CYP3A Inducers: Avoid concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inducer. Concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inducer decreases sparsentan exposure which may reduce FILSPARI efficacy.
  • Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Agents (NSAIDs), Including Selective Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) Inhibitors: Monitor for signs of worsening renal function with concomitant use with NSAIDs (including selective COX-2 inhibitors). In patients with volume depletion (including those on diuretic therapy) or with impaired kidney function, concomitant use of NSAIDs (including selective COX-2 inhibitors) with drugs that antagonize the angiotensin II receptor may result in deterioration of kidney function, including possible kidney failure. These effects are usually reversible.
  • CYP2B6, 2C9, and 2C19 Substrates: Monitor for efficacy of concurrently administered CYP2B6, 2C9, and 2C19 substrates and consider dosage adjustment in accordance with the Prescribing Information. Sparsentan is a weak inducer of CYP2B6 and 2C9, and a moderate inducer of 2C19. Sparsentan decreases exposure of these substrates, which may reduce efficacy related to these substrates.
  • P-gp Substrates: Monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates with narrow therapeutic indices when co-administered with FILSPARI. FILSPARI is a weak P-gp inhibitor and may increase plasma concentrations of P-gp substrate drugs.
  • Agents Increasing Serum Potassium: Monitor serum potassium frequently in patients treated with FILSPARI and other agents that increase serum potassium. Concomitant use of FILSPARI with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, or other drugs that raise serum potassium levels may result in hyperkalemia.

Please see the full Prescribing Information, including BOXED WARNING, for additional Important Safety Information.

data.title: Robbins LLP Reminds PZZA Investors of the Pending Class Action Lawsuit; Harmed Investors Should Contact the Firm for Information About Leading the Class Action Against Papa John's International, Inc.
data.description:
Robbins LLP Reminds PZZA Investors of the Pending Class Action Lawsuit; Harmed Investors Should Contact the Firm for Information About Leading the Class Action Against Papa John's International, Inc.

Robbins LLP Reminds PZZA Investors of the Pending Class Action Lawsuit; Harmed Investors Should Contact the Firm for Information About Leading the Class Action Against Papa John's International, Inc.

PR Newswire

SAN DIEGO, Oct. 23, 2026

SAN DIEGO, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP reminds investors that a class action was filed on behalf of all persons and entities who purchased or otherwise acquired Papa John's International, Inc. (NASDAQ: PZZA) common stock between August 7, 2025 and August 5, 2026 (the "Class Period"). Papa John's is a global chain pizza company that operates and franchises restaurants in North America and various international markets.

The complaint alleges that Papa John's misled investors regarding its business prospects in connection with its sales, dividend, and 2026 financial outlook.

Investors who suffered significant losses during the Class Period may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit and should contact Robbins LLP for information before the November 2, 2026, lead plaintiff deadline.

Why Was Papa John's Sued?

According to the complaint, during the class period, defendants created the false impression that they possessed reliable information pertaining to the effectiveness and ongoing impact of the Company's strategic transformation as well as their resulting projected growth outlook for the North American region, while also minimizing risk against their projections from cautious consumer sentiment, competition woes, promotional seasonality, and more general macroeconomic fluctuation. In truth, Papa Johns' strategic transformation was taking considerably longer than the projections had suggested; the Company was simply ill equipped to "meet the consumer where they're at."

Why Did PZZA Stock Drop?

On August 6, 2026, Papa John's announced an 8.3% decrease in North American comparable sales, the suspension of its dividend, and a sharp reduction in its 2026 outlook from a 3% decline in North American comparable sales at the midpoint to a 7% annual decline. The Company attributed its strategic shift and guidance reset on the soft consumer trends and the execution of Papa Johns' own turnaround efforts, admitting they were unable to "meet the consumer as much as [they] should have," and the rebuilt innovation pipeline was "not bringing in as many new customers" as had been expected.

On this news, the price of Papa Johns' common stock declined dramatically. From a closing market price of $29.75 per share on August 5, 2026, Papa Johns' stock price fell to $24.64 per share on August 6, 2026, a decline of about 17.18% in the span of just a single day.

Who May Be Eligible to Participate in the Papa Johns' Class Action?

The lawsuit seeks to represent investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Papa John's common stock between August 7, 2025 and August 5, 2026. Investors who suffered losses during that period may have legal rights under the federal securities laws.

What Is a Lead Plaintiff?

The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Stockholders who wish to lead the class action should contact Robbins LLP before the November 2, 2026, lead plaintiff deadline.

Serving as lead plaintiff is not required to share in any potential recovery. Investors who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members if the case proceeds and later resolves successfully.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis.

Why Robbins LLP?

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP has helped restore more than $2 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history. 

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

To be notified if a class action against Papa John's International, Inc. settles or to receive free alerts when corporate executives engage in wrongdoing, sign up for Stock Watch today.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the Papa John's International, Inc. securities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

Attorney Advertising. Past results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

Kelly Rush, CIO of global real estate securities, will remain as co-portfolio manager of the Fund and, effective October 23, 2026, Laura Rank, managing director and portfolio manager, and Jason Haigh, portfolio manager, will serve as co-portfolio managers. There will be no changes to the Fund’s investment objectives or investment policies in connection with Peterson’s retirement.

data.title: 'I don't feel sorry for myself': I'm 64 and will be renting for the rest of my life. Is that so bad?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'I married a wonderful man with a good income. He left his job due to health issues and suffered a massive stroke at 53.'

"I'm not complaining and not feeling sorry for myself." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

As the renter in his 50s pointed out (I lost my home in the 'Great Recession.' I rent in my 50s. Why is that judged as failure?), some ill-timed circumstances can change our financial futures in unexpected ways. I am a renter in my 60s. I left a bad relationship in my 40s, just before the recession hit. As house values fell, my ex ended up buying me out with a small sum.

I married a wonderful man with a good income. He left his job due to health issues and suffered a massive stroke at 53, leaving him bed-bound, with brain damage, partial paralysis, unable to communicate or speak clearly, unable to safely eat solid foods, and in diapers. My income was enough to support me but not enough to have any real savings.

He lost his employer life-insurance benefit, and we hadn't purchased a new policy. We thought we were still young and strong and had plenty of time to plan our future. I never expected life to throw me this curveball. I ended up quitting my job to stay home and care for him full-time. That was 11 years ago. I am renting a nice house in a nice neighborhood, and we are comfortable.

Though I would love to have a house that is mine, I am glad I don't have to worry about home maintenance and repairs. When my husband dies, I will be even poorer, as I will lose his Social Security income and will have only my Social Security to live on. I was able to get a $10,000 guaranteed life-insurance policy for him, which may just cover final expenses.

I'm not complaining, and I don't feel sorry for myself. I know I could have made other choices and had a different outcome. That could have been better, or it could have been worse. I accept the direction my life has taken, and I am grateful that we are comfortable and have all we need. At this point, I expect I will be renting for the remainder of my life.

There is some comfort in not being tied down to a house.

A 64-year-old Renting in Arizona

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My wife never went back to work after raising our kids. Do I have to share my retirement savings 50/50?

There are anywhere between 7 million and 10 million people in the U.S. aged 65 and over who are renters, depending on the source.

Dear Renting in Arizona,

Thank you for writing such a vulnerable and openhearted letter. Life takes unmerciful twists and turns, and financial security is not always about choices.

The end of a relationship can be devastating emotionally, but it can also deal a swift and lasting blow to your finances, especially if one party ends up with a property and the other is out in the cold with a small amount of pocket change. The average divorce lawyer will have enough files to write a gothic horror movie (which are all the rage right now, apparently). You survived and you met your second husband, and life dealt you another unwelcome turn. Medical debt is still one of the major causes of bankruptcy in America.

Mostly, as your letter illustrates, there are often rich and wonderful and challenging and even painful life stories behind terms like "renters" and "homeowners." It's easy to judge, but it's better to listen and learn from other people's experiences. Divorce, illness, economic crises, interest-rate hikes, rising house prices, job loss, educational opportunities and upbringing can all play a role. So I want to thank you for sharing such a personal story in a public forum, because sometimes there's too little kindness and willingness to understand the lives of others.

Some folks get a nice inheritance from their parents; others don't. You are, for what it's worth, part of a large minority. There are between 7 million and 10 million people in the U.S. ages 65 and over who are renters, depending on the source. Seniors are now the fastest-growing group of renters, rising by 30% between 2013 and 2023, at least according to this U.S. Census Bureau-based estimate. Some rent by choice, while others do so out of necessity. Not everyone wants to sign up to a 30-year mortgage, one they will likely never live pay off, in their 50s or 60s.

Related: My wife says we can't afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We're in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?

HOA fees and 'rent-burdened' seniors

There are also people in their 50s and 60s who see the large amount of equity in their homes and decide why leave all that money behind, why not tap that equity, rent and live a life with more freedom? This can suit a couple with the means and the willingness to live a more unpredictable lifestyle, especially in metropolitan areas. New York City, in fact, has more senior renters than millennial renters, and, yes, a growing number are classified as "rent burdened." You belong to a colorful, lively and resilient community of senior renters.

Owning a home is expensive, sometimes prohibitively so, even if you don't have to replace the roof. Homeowner-association fees have risen by 25% to roughly $135 a month from $108 in 2019, per research from Realtor.com (which is owned by the same parent company as Dow Jones, which owns MarketWatch). HOA fees are also harder to avoid: 44% of homes for sale are now subject to a monthly HOA fee, in part due to builder preferences and a preference for HOAs among some municipalities. Property taxes have also risen more than inflation.

Surviving spouses can claim up to 100% of a late spouse's Social Security, depending on when they claim, should your husband's be higher than yours and you predecease him. You may wish to look into what financial support may be available for a family caregiver, like Medicare's home-health services, in addition to Section 8 housing and housing-choice vouchers. Affordable housing is in high demand due to rising poverty rates, and it's often a complicated prospect for seniors who earn just enough to get by but not enough to qualify.

Your home does not need to be a symbol of status and financial success. After 11 years of caring for your husband, I have no doubt that you know that better than I do.

Related: 'People in the U.S. need to wake up': As a mortgage loan officer, I rejected applications from wealthy couples. Here's why.

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist on qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

More columns from Quentin Fottrell:

'I don't want to die on the sales floor': I'm 67 and earn $19.50 an hour at a big-box store. When can I finally retire?

'I am a pretty cautious person': My financial adviser wants me to invest $350,000 in a UAE data center. Is this risky?

My sister moved in with our mother, 78, and now says she deserves the $925,000 family home. Is she right?

-Quentin Fottrell

data.title: Caldwell Announces Sale of IQTalent
data.description:
TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Caldwell (TSX:CWL)(OTCQX:CWLPF), a leading retained executive search firm, today announced it has completed the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of its wholly owned subsidiary, IQTalent Partners, Inc., to WinMil, Inc. WinMil will continue to operate the business under the IQTalent name and brand.

Caldwell acquired IQTalent in 2020 to broaden its service offerings into technology-enabled recruiting solutions at the professional level. After nearly six years, Caldwell determined that the business was not meeting the firm's strategic objectives and that a sale would better align its portfolio with its long-term priorities.

"Divesting IQTalent enables us to sharpen our focus on what Caldwell does best: delivering elite executive search and advisory services to our clients," said Chris Beck, chief executive officer of Caldwell. "IQTalent has been an important part of our portfolio, and we are proud of the innovative team and platform we helped build. We believe the business is well-positioned to succeed under WinMil's ownership, and we look forward to continuing a collaborative relationship through our referral partnership."

Founded in 2009, IQTalent pioneered an on-demand recruiting services model that blends proprietary technology with human expertise to deliver scalable talent acquisition solutions.

Transaction Terms

The transaction included the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of IQTalent. Under the terms of the agreement, total consideration at closing was approximately $4.7 million, consisting of:

  • $3.2 million in cash, subject to exchange rate changes and a net working capital adjustment; and
  • 1.45 million Caldwell common shares held by David Windley and Tom Milic, who are owners of WinMil and former employees of IQTalent. The shares were valued at approximately $1.5 million, based on a simple average price of $1.05 per Caldwell share over the 20 days prior to closing. The shares have been cancelled by Caldwell, reducing total shares outstanding by approximately 4.9%.

All dollar amounts are presented in Canadian dollars.

Caldwell retains its minority equity interest in the recruitment software company HootRecruit (formerly known as IQRecruit). Caldwell also retains the ability to utilize IQTalent's remaining deferred tax assets to apply against future taxable ordinary income generated by Caldwell in the United States.

Caldwell and WinMil have also entered into a two-year referral agreement to connect clients with the firms' complementary executive search and recruiting services.

Caldwell's Board of Directors will evaluate the use of the cash proceeds as part of its capital allocation planning and expects to provide an update with the release of Caldwell's next quarterly earnings.

​​About Caldwell

Caldwell is an elite executive search firm trusted by established and growth-focused companies alike. For more than 50 years, we have partnered with clients to design and build extraordinary leadership teams. Our partners don't just place executives-they challenge assumptions, enable strategy, and prioritize long-term fit. Built on repeat clients and referrals, Caldwell delivers clarity and results without arrogance or shortcuts. Our suite of services includes executive and board level search, as well as talent strategy and assessment tools that help organizations hire the right people, then manage and inspire them to achieve maximum business results. For clients seeking substance over scale, we're the confident voice that listens-and leads. At Caldwell, our purpose is your mission.

Caldwell's common shares trade on The Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX:CWL) and trade on the OTCQX Market (OTCQX:CWLPF). For more information, visit www.caldwell.com

data.title: Black Rock Coffee Bar Continues Expansion in California with New Rancho Cucamonga Location
data.description:
Scottsdale, AZ, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Black Rock Coffee Bar, the Oregon-born boutique coffee chain celebrated for its specialty coffees, teas, smoothies, and signature Fuel® energy drinks, is growing its footprint in California with the opening of a new store in Rancho Cucamonga. 

The store, located at 11370 Fourth St, will officially open its doors on Sunday, October 25th. This opening marks Black Rock’s eighth California location and reinforces the brand’s steady expansion across the state. Guests can enjoy the following specials during opening week: 

  • Sunday, October 25th: $2 Medium Drinks 
  • Monday, October 26th: BOGO Drinks 
  • Tuesday, October 27th: 50% Off a Drink w/ Food Purchase 
  • Wednesday, October 28th: Signature Grand Opening Sticker with a Purchase 
  • Thursday, October 29th: Free T-shirt with a Purchase 
  • Friday, October 30th: $2 Off Any Size Drink 

“California has been an important part of Black Rock’s growth, and we’re excited to expand in the state,” said Mark Davis, CEO of Black Rock Coffee Bar. “We look forward to becoming part of the Rancho Cucamonga community and creating a welcoming place for guests to enjoy their favorite drinks and fuel their day!” 

 

Guests can also take advantage of the Black Rock Rewards app, where every purchase—whether in-store, online, or through the app—earns “bolts” that can be redeemed for free beverages. Recent menu additions, like Black Rock’s protein-packed Egg Bites, are also included in the program. 

 

Black Rock Coffee Bar is beloved for its handcrafted beverages, including the Caramel Blondie, a sweet and creamy signature blend; the Mexican Mocha, a spicy twist with hints of vanilla, almond, and cinnamon; and the Jackhammer, a vanilla mocha with an extra double shot; as well as its in-house developed Fuel energy drink, customizable with over 20 fruit flavors.  These can be enjoyed alongside sweet and savory food items, including the recently launched Grilled Cheese and Pumpkin Blondie Cake Pop. For an extra kick of protein, guests can add Black Rock’s new Protein Cold Foam, Protein Boosted Milk or Protein Boost to their drinks. 

 

In addition to Black Rock menu staples, guests can enjoy limited-time offerings like the Pumpkin Spiced Latte, Pumpkin Blondie, and Pumpkin Spice Cookie Latte with Cookie Butter Cold Foam. The brand’s Fall Remix seasonal drinks are also now available, featuring the Caramel Apple Butter Shaken Espresso, Cinnamon Bun Latte, and Spellbound Berry Fuel, offering a mix of nostalgic and refreshing flavors.  

 

For more information, visit https://br.coffee/ and follow @blackrockcoffeebar on Facebook and Instagram, and @blackrockcoffeeofficial on TikTok for updates on new locations, promotions, and seasonal offerings. 

 

About Black Rock Coffee Bar  

Black Rock Coffee Bar is a national boutique coffee shop that is known for its premium roasted coffees, teas, smoothies and flavorful Fuel® energy drinks. Founded as a family owned and operated business in Oregon in 2008, Black Rock Coffee Bar has grown to over 200 retail locations in seven states. The Black Rock culture prides itself on not only being a positive force for the communities it serves, but also the team members that fuel their locations day in and day out. An important aspect of their team mission is to recognize those that go above and beyond by displaying the 4G’s of Black Rock - grit, growth, gratitude, and grace. For more information, visit https://br.coffee/.

data.title: Sparta Capital Ltd. Provides Corporate Update on Reinstatement Review, Financial Statement Corrections and Governance Matters
data.description:
TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Sparta Group (TSXV:SAY) (the "Corporation", the "Company", "Sparta Group", "Sparta Capital", "SAY.V" or "Sparta") reports on the status of the ongoing review by the TSX Venture Exchange (the "Exchange") of the Company's application for reinstatement to trading of its common shares and sets out clarifications and corrections to previously disclosed information.

Trading Reinstatement

The Exchange has completed its reinstatement review. The Company's common shares will be reinstated to trading soon.

Current Loans Receivable Clarification

The Company is clarifying the nature and settlement of a balance previously described in its financial statements as a current loan receivable owed by 1123747 B.C. Ltd., a company associated with a director of Re-ECO Tech Electronic Conversions Ltd. ("Re-ECO"), the Company's majority voting-controlled subsidiary. The Company advanced the underlying funds in connection with giving Re-ECO, through its ERS International division, access to the Nano Sorter AI-based recycling and sorting equipment for use in its e-waste processing and IT Asset Disposition operations. The balance was non-interest-bearing and included no interest, foreign exchange, or top-up component. The balance increased from $80,907 September 30, 2025, to $81,420 on December 31, 2025, and to $84,389 on March 31, 2026, because of G Suite subscription fees and legal fees paid by the Company on behalf of 1123747 B.C. Ltd., net of a repayment of $583. On June 30, 2026, the balance was settled in full through the transfer of the Nano Sorter equipment to Re-ECO, and no cash was received by the Company in connection with the settlement. The balance was accordingly reduced to $nil on June 30, 2026, as disclosed in Note 11 to the Company's unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the three and nine months ended June 30, 2026, filed on SEDAR+ on August 28, 2026 (the "Q3 2026 Interim Statements"). The Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows in the Q3 2026 Interim Statements presented the $84,389 settlement as a source of cash under investing activities. Because no cash was received, that amount should not have been presented as a cash inflow, and will instead be removed from investing activities and disclosed as a non-cash transaction. The recorded balance is correctly stated at $nil. The corrected cash flow presentation, together with note disclosure describing the non-cash settlement of the balance through the transfer of equipment, will be reflected in the Company's audited annual consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, required to be filed on or before January 28, 2027 under section 4.2(2) of National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations.

Correction to Marketing Expense Disclosure and Related Internal Controls

The Company is correcting a negative (credit) balance of $(65,561) in marketing (business development) expense that appeared in its unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the six months ended March 31, 2026. The negative balance resulted from the reversal in fiscal 2026 of a commission accrual recorded at September 30, 2025, relating to revenues earned in fiscal 2025 that were not invoiced or paid until fiscal 2026, which accrual was included in business development expense of $155,683 in the Company's audited financial statements for the year ended September 30, 2025. The $(65,561) balance is a net amount, comprising the reversal of the commission accrual in the amount of $65,74, partially offset by $180 of marketing services expense recorded during the six months ended March 31, 2026. The accrual was reversed to avoid double counting when the related commission invoices were received. Commissions for the six months ended March 31, 2026, were, however, still recorded in consulting fees under the Company's prior practice, so no commission expense was recorded in the marketing account to offset the reversal. The Company has since separated commissions paid to parties that generate sales from fees paid to consultants who provide outside expertise, and the year-to-date commissions were reclassified from consulting fees to marketing expense on June 30, 2026. The negative balance was not attributable to new projects or changes in marketing activity. The three-month business development expense of $664,946 for the period ended June 30, 2026, principally reflects that reclassification of year-to-date commission expenses. The cumulative amount of $599,385 for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, is lower than the three-month amount because the accrual reversal reduced the year-to-date balance. Following its annual general meeting on May 21, 2026, the Company constituted a new Audit Committee (described below) that reviews the Company's quarterly financial statements prior to filing, and the Company has implemented additional review procedures for expense coding, related-party identification and TSXV filing requirements to reduce the risk of similar classification errors recurring.

Disclosure Regarding Share Issuances Prior to Receipt of Funds

In connection with a September 2017 convertible debenture financing, related receipts recorded in 2018, and a 2023 financing, the Company issued common shares prior to receiving, or without ultimately receiving, the related funds in full.

Following closing of the Company's 2023 private placement, subscription receivables totaling $99,500 were outstanding, comprising $79,500 relating to the 2023 private placement and $20,000 carried forward from the earlier financing records. Of the $79,500 relating to the 2023 private placement: (i) $25,000 was collected on January 15, 2024 from ERS International; (ii) $30,000 was owed by Alyn Patterson, the Company's Chief Financial Officer at the time, who was issued 1,000,000 common shares for which payment was not received, an amount disclosed as a related-party amount due from the Chief Financial Officer in the Company's annual filings for fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025; and (iii) $24,500 was not received. The $20,000 balance traces to a $365,000 convertible debenture financing completed in September 2017. The historical records initially described $75,000 as receivable and subsequently recorded $85,000 as a receivable under "conversion of debentures"; $65,000 was collected between October and December 2018 and recorded as private-placement proceeds, although no shares were issued for that receipt. The remaining $74,500, being $30,000, $24,500 and $20,000, was written off by the Company as uncollectible and recorded as bad debt expense. All common shares issued in respect of the written-off receivables remain issued and outstanding. The share issuance records for these financings were administered by the Company's former President prior to his death in October 2023 and were not fully transferred to current management. The Company has reviewed the available transfer-agent, subscription and payment records and will continue to reconcile the historical accounting entries as additional predecessor-management records become available.

The Company has adopted the practice, effective for all issuances going forward, that it will not issue, or characterize as issued or pending in connection with a financing, common shares until (i) in the case of a private placement, applicable subscription funds have been received and cleared, in accordance with TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.1 - Private Placements; or (ii) in the case of a debt settlement or services-based issuance, the news release announcing the issuance expressly discloses that the shares are issued for non-cash consideration and does not characterize the transaction as a "private placement," in accordance with TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.3 - Shares for Debt. As additional remedial and corrective measures, the Company has designated its Chief Financial Officer as responsible for confirming that subscription funds have been received and cleared before instructing the Company's transfer agent to issue any shares in connection with a private placement, and the Company's Audit Committee will review share issuance records, including any outstanding subscription receivables, as part of its quarterly review of the Company's financial statements.

Clarification of October 2, 2024, Private Placement ($102,030)

The Company is correcting the characterization of the transaction announced in its news release dated October 2, 2024, in the amount of $102,030. That amount reflected the aggregate deemed value of common shares issued by the Company in October 2024, and did not represent cash proceeds raised by way of a private placement, as follows: (i) 2,601,510 common shares (together with 2,601,510 warrants exercisable at $0.10 per share for eighteen months) issued at a deemed value of $52,030 (comprising $50,000 principal and $2,030 accrued interest) to Gerald T. Miller in settlement of outstanding debt; and (ii) 2,500,000 common shares (together with 2,500,000 warrants exercisable at $0.10 per share for eighteen months) issued at a deemed value of $50,000 to Advisir Ventures Ltd. for advertising-related services. The Company's October 2, 2024, news release stated that proceeds would be used to fund audit, legal and licence fees; the Company is clarifying that no cash proceeds were received in connection with these share issuances, and that the previously disclosed use of proceeds does not apply to this transaction. Mr. Miller is the Company's external legal counsel; he has never been a director or officer of the Company and does not hold more than 10% of the Company's voting shares. Advisir Ventures Ltd. is an unrelated, arm's-length party to the Company.

Catch-Up Regulatory Filings

In connection with the reinstatement review, the Company confirms that it has made or submitted the following filings to the Exchange:

  • Convertible Debentures: a historical Form 4B filing and supplemental submission under TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.1 in respect of the Company's outstanding 8% unsecured convertible debentures. The original financing was announced by news releases dated November 3, 2021, and December 3, 2021, and an extension was announced by news release dated January 14, 2022. Between November 2021 and February 2022, the Company issued 55 unsecured convertible debentures at a price of $5,000 per debenture for aggregate gross proceeds of $275,000. Each debenture bore interest at 8% per annum, matured two years from its date of issuance and was convertible into units at $0.20 per unit, with each unit consisting of one common share and one-half of one common share purchase warrant. On October 5, 2022, the Company extended the conversion period and modified the conversion terms for $200,000 face value of existing debentures and issued an additional $150,000 face value of debentures convertible at $0.05 per share until October 5, 2023. In February 2023, a $20,000 debenture was converted into 666,667 common shares. In September 2023, one debenture was increased from $100,000 to $200,000 and the maturity dates of all outstanding debentures were extended to November 2024, resulting in $355,000 of principal outstanding. No separate news releases were identified for the October 2022 changes or the September 2023 amendment. The October 2022 changes and the September amendment have been submitted to the Exchange as part of the Company's catch-up filings and remain subject to Exchange acceptance. The debentures matured in November 2024 and are currently in default and classified as current liabilities. The conversion rights and related warrant entitlements have expired. Consistent with subsection 1.6(h)(ii) of Form 51-102F1, the Company has updated the liquidity risk disclosure in its MD&A to reflect the default status of the debentures. The Company is actively exploring restructuring options, and any future restructuring, extension, refinancing or settlement of the debentures will be submitted to the Exchange for acceptance, as required.
  • Disposition of the Sold Entities: a submission under section 3.1 of TSX Venture Exchange Policy 5.3 - Acquisitions and Dispositions of Non-Cash Assets, addressing the Company's September 30, 2025, disposition of its interests in six non-operating subsidiaries to 2420604 Ontario Limited for aggregate consideration of $5, together with the related threshold analysis.The subsidiaries were non-operational and were generating ongoing administrative expenses to maintain. The Company disposed of them to eliminate those costs and liabilities of the subsidiaries and recognized a one-time gain of disposal. The disposition was unanimously approved by the Company's board of directors, then comprised of Tony Peticca, Shawn Leon and Peter Quattro. Gerald T. Miller, the Company's external legal counsel, is the sole shareholder, director and officer of 2420604 Ontario Limited. Mr. Miller has never been an officer or director of the Company, and Mr. Miller and 2420604 Ontario Limited are arm's-length parties to the Company. The disposition remains subject to acceptance by the Exchange
  • Disposition of Re-ECO: a submission under section 3.1 of TSX Venture Exchange Policy 5.3 addressing the Company's February 3, 2025, disposition of 120,000 Class B Special Shares of Re-ECO, representing 12 percentage points of the Company's equity interest in Re-ECO (reducing the Company's equity interest from 20% to 8%), to 1123747 B.C. Ltd. for cash consideration of $250,000. The disposition was undertaken as part of a corporate realignment and to provide working capital and was unanimously approved by the Company's board of directors, then comprised of Tony Peticca, Shawn Leon and Peter Quattro. The disposition of the Re-ECO Class B Special Shares remains subject to acceptance by the Exchange. 1123747 B.C. Additional Disclosure - Continued Listing Requirements

The Company does not currently meet the working capital criterion of the Exchange's Continued Listing Requirements. Based on the Company's unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements as of June 30, 2026, the Company has a working capital deficiency of $137,848 and does not meet the Exchange's six-month general and administrative expense requirement of approximately $4,612,000.

The Company intends to address its working capital deficiency and work toward satisfying the Exchange's Continued Listing Requirements through a combination of operating performance and new financing. The Company's working capital position has fluctuated with the cyclical nature of ERS International's recycling and IT asset disposition business and has improved significantly from the position that existed when trading was suspended. The Company returned to profitability in fiscal 2025. Although ERS International's revenue and profitability declined in fiscal 2026, the expenses incurred during that period included investments made in anticipation of a return to profitable growth in fiscal 2027, which management expects to have a positive impact on the Company's working capital position. Following the resumption of trading, the Company also intends to pursue an equity financing at the corporate level, separate from ERS International, targeting gross proceeds of approximately $500,000 to $1,500,000. The final size, pricing, structure and timing of the financing have not been determined and will be subject to market conditions and applicable regulatory approvals and Exchange acceptance. The Company has had preliminary discussions with prospective investors and has received non-binding expressions of interest, but no definitive subscription agreements or other commitments have been entered into. If completed, the Company expects to use the net proceeds to provide working capital and fund ongoing corporate operations and growth initiatives. The Company also intends to complete the proposed shares-for-debt transaction described in item (f) above and to explore a restructuring, extension, refinancing or settlement of the $355,000 convertible debentures in each case subject to required shareholder approval and Exchange acceptance. There can be no assurance that the Company will complete any financing or other measure, or that it will meet the Continued Listing Requirements, and if it does not, the Exchange may transfer the Company's listing to the NEX board or take other action under its policies.

About Sparta Capital Ltd.

Sparta Capital Ltd. is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol "SAY."
